title: Comb-textured buttercream
subtitle: serrated scraper technique for ridged and striped sides
excerpt: A serrated cake comb or icing scraper dragged around a freshly iced cake creates evenly spaced ridges in the buttercream. The pattern can be horizontal stripes, chevron, or vertical ridges depending on the scraper shape and how it is moved. This gives a much more refined look than a smooth scrape with a straight-edged scraper, and the ridges catch a second colour if you fill them in after the first pass.
sourceNotes: Textured buttercream finishes with icing combs have been used in commercial cake decorating since at least the mid-20th century. The serrated scraper (or icing comb) is a standard bakery tool used both for cleaning and patterning frosted cakes. The two-colour ridged technique, where ridges are piped in a contrasting colour and smoothed flush, appeared in the decorating competition world in the 2010s and was later adopted widely in home baking. The basic comb-scrape technique itself requires only the scraper and a turntable.

content.text: A comb-textured buttercream finish uses a serrated scraper to cut evenly spaced horizontal ridges around the sides of a cake. It requires a crumb coat, a full coating of buttercream, and a turntable, the scraper stays still while the cake rotates. The texture reads beautifully at distance and takes a second colour well if you pipe into the ridges and smooth again.

Apply a thin crumb coat of buttercream over the entire cake using a straight palette knife. This seals in loose crumbs so they don't mix into the top coat. Refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes until the crumb coat is firm enough not to move when touched.

Apply a generous layer of buttercream to the sides, spreading it thicker than the finished result will be, the comb will remove a significant amount. Spread buttercream across the top of the cake as well, slightly higher than the final level. Use a straight-edged scraper held at a 90° angle to the cake and spin the turntable to smooth the sides to a rough cylinder. This doesn't need to be perfect, just broadly even.

Hold the serrated comb against the side of the cake at a 90° angle, teeth pressed lightly into the buttercream. Start the turntable rotating at a steady speed and hold the comb steady, pressing just firmly enough that the teeth cut through to but not past the crumb coat. Complete the rotation in one smooth movement. Where the comb lifts at the end of the rotation you'll have a seam, blend this with a clean palette knife tip using a short upward stroke. Refrigerate for 20 minutes before adding any decoration on top.

After the initial comb pass, pipe a contrasting colour of buttercream into each groove using a small round piping tip. Then hold a straight-edged scraper against the cake and spin the turntable again, removing the excess so only the grooves are filled. The result is crisp alternating coloured stripes visible in the channels of the pattern.
